prophet: One day the Prophet ﷺ climbed a small hill and called the Quraysh. When they came together, he asked, 'If I told you an enemy would come at morning or evening, would you believe me?' They said, 'Yes.' He said: 'I am warning you before a very hard punishment.' Abu Lahab said: 'You gathered us for this? May you be ruined!' Then Allah sent down this surah. (Sahih al-Bukhari, from Ibn Abbas.)

Rabi'ah ibn Abbad said that before he was Muslim, he saw the Prophet ﷺ in a market saying: 'People, say there is no god but Allah, and you will win.' A man with a bright face walked behind him, saying: 'He is a liar!' People said, 'That is his uncle, Abu Lahab.' (Ahmad.)
scholars: Ibn Kathir says Abu Lahab was an uncle of the Prophet ﷺ. His real name was Abdul-Uzza. People called him Abu Lahab because his face was so bright, like fire. He hurt the Prophet ﷺ a lot.
Ibn Kathir says the first part is a dua against him, and the second part tells what happened to him.
Ibn Abbas, Aisha, Mujahid and others said 'what he earned' means his children. (Told by Ibn Kathir.)
Ibn Mas'ud said Abu Lahab said, 'If what my nephew says is true, I will save myself from the punishment with my money and my children.' So Allah sent this ayah. (Told by Ibn Kathir.)
Ibn Kathir says 'a Fire with flames' is a fire with very strong fire and burning.
The book Al-Jalalayn says his nickname comes from his bright red face.
Ibn Kathir says his wife was Umm Jamil. Her name was Arwa, a daughter of Harb, and the sister of Abu Sufyan. She helped her husband in not believing and in being stubborn.
Ibn Abbas and others said she put thorns in the path of the Prophet ﷺ. (Told by Ibn Kathir.)

Asma, daughter of Abu Bakr, told that when this surah came down, Umm Jamil came with a stone in her hand. The Prophet ﷺ was sitting by the Kaaba with Abu Bakr. Abu Bakr said, 'She is coming, and I am afraid she will see you.' The Prophet ﷺ said, 'She will not see me,' and he read some Quran. She stood in front of Abu Bakr but could not see the Prophet ﷺ. (Told by Ibn Kathir.)
Ibn Kathir says 'masad' is a rope made of fibers. Mujahid and Urwah said this means a rope from the fire. She will carry firewood in the Fire and throw it on her husband.
The book Tanwir al-Miqbas (from Ibn Abbas) says it can also mean an iron chain on her neck.
